A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EEdit and contain readable main text and supplementary material. Algorithms, equations, tables, proofs, and image galleries can be matched reliably despite changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing experiments, efficiency measurements, and SLoC/TIP/ISS ablations, including supplementary Tables 4–5 and qualitative galleries.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and expands the quality and efficiency comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: The SLoC scoring and cache updates, TIP preprocessing, ISS procedure, and algorithm steps are retained. Clarified notation in Algorithm 1 and revised wording for the neighborhood parameter K do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use PIE-Bench, TF-ICON, and DragBench-SR/DR for the same editing tasks. The Redux image-variation examples already appear in v1's appendix. No additional dataset, task, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 adds standalone RF-inv, RF-Edit, and Flow-Edit rows to Table 1 while retaining the earlier comparators. These FLUX-based comparisons substantially broaden the main evaluation beyond the earlier SD/PixArt competitors; prior citations or use of RF-inversion within EEdit did not supply these standalone comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 expands its quality-only comparison to include FLOPs and latency across editing methods. These metrics already appeared elsewhere, so this is a limited extension of evaluation scope. The stated 28-step setup, guidance ratio of 7.0, datasets, and H20 hardware remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The spatial-caching, inversion-skipping, TIP/ISS, cache-comparator, and hidden-state analyses are retained, including Tables 2–5. Figure 2 relabels and rearranges the existing demonstration; it does not introduce another ablation or new robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The fixed-seed discussion remains part of the TIP equivalence proof. Removing an unquantified reference to 'random fluctuations' does not change a statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds complete results for three flow-based comparators and substantial new efficiency data. For example, RF-Edit has CLIP-T 26.64 and latency 26.23 s; newly listed InfEdit latency is 2.90 s versus SLoC+ISS at 4.60 s. Existing Table 1 quality scores and Tables 2–5 remain unchanged, so this expands comparative evidence rather than showing improved EEdit performance across versions.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow equations, neighborhood and cache-frequency definitions, and supplementary TIP equivalence proof are retained. The notation clarifications do not change mathematical assumptions, derivations, or conclusions.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same central claims about spatial and temporal redundancy, the three acceleration components, near-lossless editing, average 2.46× acceleration, and acceleration up to 10.96× against selected editing methods. The expanded comparisons do not redefine the stated contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of background preservation, temporal redundancy, and TIP's losslessness remain. The new appendix remarks on watermarking and broader controllable-generation applications are general future-work statements, without specific failure conditions, developed limitations, or substantive reinterpretations of results.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's supplementary hardware/software specification section, including CPU, operating-system, Python, and library versions. Conversely, Table 1 newly identifies baseline model families and parameter counts. Main inference settings, GPU information, metric backbones, and code/data links remain available.

R1.justification: New supplementary Section 12 substantially expands citation coverage across editing, video generation, acceleration, watermarking, and controllable generation, including VideoGrain, FastVAR, IntLoRA, WMAdapter, and EasyControl. This broadens the research context, although discussion is mostly brief and the central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the narrative structure are retained. v3 makes localized terminology and notation edits, shortens the TIP discussion, adds acknowledgments and supplementary related-work subsections, and removes the supplementary implementation section with corresponding renumbering.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned with quality/efficiency groups, model information, and highlighted rows. Figure 2 is rearranged and corrects reversed inversion/denoising labels; Figure 6 changes FLOPs labels to TFLOPs. Other figures and appendix galleries remain substantially unchanged, with localized table and text reflow.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 1 makes quality–efficiency tradeoffs more assessable through relevant FLUX comparators, cost measurements, and explicit model identities. Correcting Figure 2's reversed labels also improves clarity. These gains outweigh the limited loss of reproducibility from removing environment specifications, but the unchanged method, theory, and ablations keep the overall improvement modest.
